title: Does spatial structure protect evolving populations from extinction?
question: Do well-mixed populations (offspring born anywhere) go extinct more often than viscous ones (offspring born near their parents), and do they evolve higher aggression?
background: Exploratory observation in Experiment C2: 7/12 well-mixed populations went extinct vs 2/12 viscous (Fisher p = 0.09, not significant). In the one surviving well-mixed+learning run the aggression gene reached 3.2 vs ~1.9 in viscous runs. This mirrors Kerr et al. (2006, Nature): restricted migration favours restraint and avoids a tragedy of the commons. This study re-tests it with more seeds.

hypotheses.statement: Well-mixed populations go extinct more often
The aggression gene evolves higher in well-mixed populations (surviving runs)
